Aquatic Viper Vine.description:
A voracious, flesh-eating carnivore, the viper vine has a single enormous blossom arising from a thick, leafy tangle of snakelike vines. When the plant senses the approach of suitable prey through its sensitive, shallow-buried root system, it rises up like an agitated snake and unfurls its brightly colored bloom, an act that releases a cloud of mind-numbing pollen.

Since viper vines gain nourishment by consuming creatures rather than through photosynthesis and absorbing nutrients from the soil, they have developed rudimentary locomotion and can drag themselves along the ground with tentacle-like roots. They even have a form of rudimentary sentience, allowing them to both discern differences in prey and make limited tactical decisions, while also avoiding creatures that are particularly large or dangerous looking.

The area around viper vine hunting grounds is often strewn with the partially devoured remains of victims. It's not unusual to find the rotting corpses of wild animals, ill-fated adventurers, and even giants in the plant's immediate vicinity, along with a scattering of incidental treasure left behind on the corpses. A viper vine rarely returns to the carcass of a creature it killed earlier, preferring to hunt fresh meat.

6OlSYo00X1yt0HPu.name: Cold Vulnerability

mlxDBk3SvOubNTSz.description:
The viper vine releases a @Template[emanation|distance:60] of invisible pollen that stays in the air for 5 rounds unless dispersed by a moderate or stronger wind. Each creature that enters or starts its turn in the area must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:33|options:area-effect,inflicts:sickened,inflicts:fascinated,inflicts:stupefied] save or be captivated.

The viper vine can't use Captivating Pollen for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Captivating Pollen]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Captivating Pollen for 24 hours.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated}, and it must spend each of its actions to move closer to the viper vine as expediently as possible while avoiding obvious dangers. If a captivated creature is adjacent to the viper vine, it stays still and doesn't act. It ceases to be fascinated if it's no longer in the pollen aura at the end of its turn.

Critical Failure As failure, plus the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 24 hours.
mlxDBk3SvOubNTSz.name: Captivating Pollen

Aquatic Viper Vine.name: Aquatic Viper Vine

Avernal Vortex.description: The edges of the extraplanar tunnel seem to writhe with malevolence, as if preventing unwanted souls from passing through.
Avernal Vortex.hazardDisable: @Check[arcana|dc:50] (master) or @Check[religion|dc:50] (master) to allow the group to traverse along the portal tunnel; six total successes are required to complete the journey; a PC who succeeds at a @Check[acrobatics|dc:48], @Check[athletics|dc:48], or @Check[survival|dc:48] check as a 2-action activity grants themselves a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and saves against the hazard's routine for 1 round (on a critical success, they can also grant this bonus to one other PC)
Avernal Vortex.hazardReset: Once the PCs pass through the portal tunnel and arrive in Hell, the Avernal vortex ends and doesn't reset.
Avernal Vortex.hazardRoutine:
(1 action; divine) The Avernal vortex churns across the portal tunnel, stopping the PCs from reaching their ultimate destination. In the first round, the vortex takes an action to attempt to dispel all beneficial spells on all creatures in the tunnel, scouring them with Hellfire. The vortex has a counteract modifier of [[/r 1d20+43 #Counteract]]{+43} and a counteract rank of 10, and rolls separately for each spell. On a success, the target creature takes @Damage[4d6[fire]] damage with a @Check[fortitude|dc:45|basic] save (this has the divine, fire, and unholy traits).

In the second round, the vortex attempts to instill a dread of tumbling forever through the tunnel to those within it; each creature takes @Damage[6d6[persistent,mental]] damage with a @Check[will|dc:45|basic] save (this is an emotion and mental effect). Once a creature ends its persistent mental damage (or if they avoided the persistent damage), they can reach and escape the tunnel.

In all subsequent rounds, the vortex releases bolts of acid, cold, fire, and electricity. It makes one vortex bolt Strike against each creature in the tunnel.
Avernal Vortex.name: Avernal Vortex

c1qMVNtvfEFTM1Jd.name: Hell's Call

vklePDp4ChdoOuoW.description: The brimstone corps rushes forward with a hunger for battle. They Stride up to twice their Speed. At the end of their movement, each enemy within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] takes @Damage[(2d6+5)[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage, with a @Check[reflex|dc:30|basic|options:area-effect] save.
vklePDp4ChdoOuoW.name: First-class Charge

Brimstone Corps.name: Brimstone Corps

Captivating Gem.description: The floating gem flares with inner radiance, sending out beams of light to captivate and drain the vitality from all who approach.
Captivating Gem.hazardDisable: @Check[arcana|dc:35] (expert), @Check[occultism|dc:35] (expert), or @Check[religion|dc:35] (expert) to unravel the magical matrix within the gem, @Check[crafting|dc:40] or @Check[thievery|dc:40] check to unbalance the crystal's alignment, or a @Check[athletics|dc:43] check to damage one of the gem's facets and change its geometry; two successes are required to disable the hazard
Captivating Gem.hazardRoutine: (3 actions) The captivating gem attempts uses all three of its actions to incapacitate creatures. It targets the closest creature with its Freezing Light ability, then a different creature with its facet flare Strike. If a creature has already been @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} by Freezing Light, it chooses a different target for that ability.
Captivating Gem.name: Captivating Gem

Cathilia's Meddling.description: A Hellknight on horseback shouts commands, beseeching all to return to order.
Cathilia's Meddling.hazardDisable: @Check[Hellknight Lore|dc:21] (trained) to convince the Hellknight that she's adding to chaos, or @Check[diplomacy|dc:25] to request she stop yelling
Cathilia's Meddling.hazardRoutine: (3 actions) Cathilia uses her Hellknight's Orders Strike on creatures engaged in open fighting in area A2. She randomly chooses between targets in the likely case that there are multiple combatants.
Cathilia's Meddling.name: Cathilia's Meddling

Champion of Asmodeus.description:
The deific champion is the paragon of champions, representing the truest form of devotion and dedication to a deity.

Religions inspire devout individuals to uphold their tenets.

AvhDj66mr2YhqJwo.description: When the champion becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened}, they reduce the condition value by 1 (to a minimum of 0).
AvhDj66mr2YhqJwo.name: Champion's Courage

D3y75ASOT2d7kylq.description:
Trigger An enemy damages the deific champion's ally, and both are in the deific champion's aura

Effect The ally gains resistance 14 to all damage against the triggering damage. If the enemy is within reach, the deific champion makes a melee Strike against it. Each ally in the champion's aura can spend a reaction to Strike the target with a –5 penalty.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.KzwcLwJ4c6hon0pu]{Effect: Exalted Retributive Strike}
D3y75ASOT2d7kylq.name: Exalted Retributive Strike

Qah8iLjN3hok7tMx.description:
Effect The deific champion declares their devotion to their deity and their cause. They Stride, then make a melee Strike. If the Strike hits an enemy, all allies within their champion's aura gain a +2 status bonus to attack rolls and saving throws against fear until the start of the deific champion's next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.N402OXwxrqVkcK87]{Effect: Will Not Falter}
Qah8iLjN3hok7tMx.name: Will Not Falter

en9fScCzZTAo4OaI.description: At the start of each of their turns, the deific champion gains an additional reaction they can only use to make a Reactive Strike or to Shield Block.
en9fScCzZTAo4OaI.name: Deific Reactions

gN7pHXO9N3RwzM3R.description:
Activate R (concentrate)

Trigger A creature within your reach uses a manipulate or move action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a moving action it's using

Requirements You are a master with the affixed weapon

When you activate this resin-strengthened viper skull, make a melee Strike against the triggering creature.

If you have Reactive Strike, you can activate the viper's fang as a free action.

If your attack is a critical hit and the trigger was a manipulate action, you disrupt that action.

This Strike doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike.

If you hit with this attack, the creature is exposed to viper fang venom.

Viper Fang Venom (poison)

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:32]

Maximum Duration 4 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[3d10[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1}.

ixoazJ1epK2jCK7H.description: 15 feet. Any follower of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus} in the aura knows the champion is a champion of Asmodeus. Enemies in the champion's aura take a –1 circumstance penalty to saving throws against fear. In addition, an enemy that ends its turn in the champion's aura can't reduce the value of its frightened condition below 1.
ixoazJ1epK2jCK7H.name: Champion's Aura

raqxmRxswaqs6DAA.description: In the deific champion's hands, a shield gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.bvROhtzAez0KP7Vt]{moderate reinforcing rune}, giving it Hardness 8, 84 HP, and BT 42.
raqxmRxswaqs6DAA.name: Blessed Shield

xB8qYlHLdFIjDXDe.description:
Trigger The deific champion's Hit Points are reduced to 0 for the first time that day

Effect The champion presses on, refusing to fail their god. They remain standing with 25 Hit Points.
xB8qYlHLdFIjDXDe.name: Will Not Fall

Champion of Asmodeus.name: Champion of Asmodeus

Collapsing Egorian Building.description: Tremors from the changing landscape could cause a building to collapse.
Collapsing Egorian Building.hazardDisable: @Check[athletics|dc:45] (master), @Check[crafting|dc:45] (master), or @Check[engineering-lore|dc:45] (master) to brace the structure against collapse until the end of the creature's next turn. The DC of the flat check for this round (see Routine) decreases by 4 on a success (or by 8 on a critical success). Decreasing the flat check DC to 0 stabilizes the structure, ending this hazard.
Collapsing Egorian Building.hazardReset: The building becomes susceptible to Shake to Pieces again [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds} after it's stabilized.
Collapsing Egorian Building.hazardRoutine: (1 action) The GM rolls a @Check[flat|dc:11], decreasing the DC as noted above. If the check fails, dust and debris fall within the building and 30 feet around it, providing concealment for 1 round and dealing @Damage[10d6[bludgeoning]] damage to 1d4 randomly chosen targets in the area (@Check[reflex|dc:40|basic] save); a target that critically fails this save is also knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. If the flat check critically fails, the effect is the same, but damage from the debris increases to 16d6, it affects 2d4 randomly chosen targets, and a creature that critically fails its save is knocked prone and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by the rubble ([[/act escape dc=40]], [[/act force-open dc=44]]).
Collapsing Egorian Building.name: Collapsing Egorian Building

Crowncrusher Bulwark.description: Stone bulwarks are slow and steady constructs typically carved from marble or granite. They're often made to serve as works of art when at rest, so some magical crafters employ master sculptors to ensure their constructs make beautiful statues. Older stone bulwarks might be weathered, with scuffed or cracked surfaces or missing noses and digits, but this weathering is largely cosmetic and doesn't adversely impact the bulwark's functionality.

AQkAJLS7IVqr7GLQ.description: Any creature hit by the stone bulwark's fist or rock Strike is affected by a @Check[fortitude|dc:30] @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gPvtmKMRpg9I9D7H]{Earthbind} spell.
AQkAJLS7IVqr7GLQ.name: Binding Stone

bKmTRJI4PjS70sWZ.description: The stone bulwark Strides up to its Speed, pushing back each creature whose space it moves into and damaging them if they try to stop its movement. A creature can attempt to bar the way by succeeding at a @Check[fortitude|dc:34] save. On a critical success, the resisting creature takes no damage; otherwise it is damaged as if hit by the construct's fist.
bKmTRJI4PjS70sWZ.name: Inexorable March

bhmnG9zTS4ncYGoL.description:
20 feet.

Rocks of marble magically arise from the ground in the aura. They protect the bulwark's allies, giving each of them standard @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.other-effects.Item.I9lfZUiCwMiGogVi]{Cover}. These stones can be used for Throw Rock.

This aura automatically activates at the start of the stone bulwark's first turn in combat and deactivates at the end of combat.
bhmnG9zTS4ncYGoL.name: Statuary Aura

Crowncrusher Bulwark.name: Crowncrusher Bulwark

Crowncrusher Riot.description: A crew of anarchists rush to fight the dottari.
Crowncrusher Riot.hazardDisable: @Check[intimidation|dc:21] to force them to back down, or @Check[diplomacy|dc:25] (expert) to request that they only injure the dottari
Crowncrusher Riot.hazardRoutine: (2 actions) The rioters lob bricks and other heavy objects at any dottari excruciator divisions as an action, dealing @Damage[(2d6+10)[bludgeoning]] damage to the dottari and any adjacent creatures (@Check[reflex|dc:27|basic] save).
Crowncrusher Riot.name: Crowncrusher Riot

3I6IHSlmST1oOqIB.description: The cultist's Strikes deal an additional @Damage[1d8[mental]] damage to creatures that are injured. This additional damage increases to @Damage[1d12[mental]] if the target has fewer than half its HP remaining.
3I6IHSlmST1oOqIB.name: Amplify Torment

HgxzRMmYh2uwAX6u.description: Whenever an effect restores at least one foe within 30 feet of the cultist to the target's full Hit Points, the cultist takes @Damage[2d8[mental]] damage.
HgxzRMmYh2uwAX6u.name: Alleviation Vulnerability

0at7K4AjFK3G8g0d.description:
30 feet.

When a creature in the aura uses a vitality spell or ability, the graveknight automatically attempts to counteract it, with a counteract modifier of [[/r 1d20+0 #Counteract]]{+34}.
0at7K4AjFK3G8g0d.name: Sacrilegious Aura

38cF1L61jshQDmlz.description: The graveknight has access to the critical specialization effects of any weapons it wields.
38cF1L61jshQDmlz.name: Weapon Master

KmICYlzCE1ME55yI.description:
HP 125; AC 40, Fort +32, Ref +27, Will +29

The graveknight summons a supernatural mount, as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WPKJOhEihhcIm2uQ]{Marvelous Mount} heightened to a rank equal to half the graveknight's level. Unlike marvelous mount, the steed's AC and saving throw bonuses are all 4 lower than the graveknight's, and the steed has one-third the graveknight's Hit Points (rounded down).

If the steed is destroyed, the graveknight must wait 1 hour before using this ability again.
KmICYlzCE1ME55yI.name: Phantom Mount

cBDtRsQ4wVdePGAV.description:
When a graveknight is destroyed, their armor rebuilds their body over the course of [[/gmr 1d10]] days—or more quickly if the armor is worn by a living host. If the body is destroyed before then, the process restarts.

A graveknight can only be permanently destroyed by obliterating their armor (such as with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.r7ihOgKv19eJQnik]{Disintegrate}), transporting it to the Forge of Creation, or throwing it into the heart of a volcano.
cBDtRsQ4wVdePGAV.name: Rejuvenation

th3Wu4NaFeWUJFxw.description: Any weapon the graveknight wields or unarmed attack the graveknight uses gains the effects of the greater fearsome weapon rune, deals an additional 1d6 mental damage, and functions as a +1 striking weapon rune.
th3Wu4NaFeWUJFxw.name: Ruinous Weapons

ub77qitwY5uGch2Z.description:
This curse affects anyone who wears a graveknight's armor for at least 1 hour

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:42] save

Onset 1 hour

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} and can't remove armor (1 day)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 2}, –10-foot status penalty to Speeds, and can't remove armor (1 day)

Stage 3 dies and transforms into the armor's graveknight.
ub77qitwY5uGch2Z.name: Graveknight's Curse

yRQarBjXLqAO1E5c.description:
The graveknight unleashes a @Template[cone|distance:30] of energy. Creatures in the area take @Damage[21d6[mental]] with a @Check[will|dc:40|basic|options:area-effect] save.

The graveknight can use this ability once every [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Devastating Blast]] rounds.
yRQarBjXLqAO1E5c.name: Devastating Blast

Deadly Spinning Blade Pillar.description: A spinning metal pole covered in deadly blades is hidden in the ceiling, connected to several trigger plates around the room and a hidden control panel built into the bed frame.
Deadly Spinning Blade Pillar.hazardDisable: @Check[thievery|dc:39] (master) three times on a pillar, or @Check[thievery|dc:37] (master) twice on the control panel deactivates the whole trap. Breaking the control panel prevents anyone from disabling the trap using the control panel and prevents the trap from deactivating automatically (see Reset below)
Deadly Spinning Blade Pillar.hazardReset: The trap deactivates and resets after 1 minute.
Deadly Spinning Blade Pillar.hazardRoutine: (3 actions) The trap uses its first action to make a spinning blade Strike against each adjacent creature. Its second action is to move in a random direction (roll 1d4 to determine the direction), and its third action to make a spinning blade Strike against each adjacent creature.
Deadly Spinning Blade Pillar.name: Deadly Spinning Blade Pillar

Rc2JoMJYOz0RUy4V.description: The vessel's unarmed attacks and any weapon they wield gain the greater flaming and greater grievous runes, and their Strikes gain the critical specialization effects of the appropriate weapon group.
Rc2JoMJYOz0RUy4V.name: Furious Flames

XZurNilz4H717f5b.description: 30 feet. When a creature ends its turn in the aura, it takes @Damage[6d6[fire]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:38|basic] save). A creature that fails this save is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 3} on a critical failure).
XZurNilz4H717f5b.name: Choking Ashes

fHyYQ7mWt3krPHrS.description: A creature that slays the deific vessel must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:41] save or be visibly marked as anathema to Asmodeus. It gains weakness 15 to unholy and takes a –2 circumstance penalty to Charisma-based skill checks against followers of Asmodeus. Creatures attempting to [[/act track]] or [[/act gather-information]] about the creature gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their checks. The mark can't be hidden but can be removed by participating in an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.7Fd4lxozd11MQ55N]{Atone} ritual led by a worshipper of Asmodeus who's 15th level or higher.
fHyYQ7mWt3krPHrS.name: Mark of Fate

Diabolic Vigor.description: Tendrils of infernal energy reach out from the Inferno Gate like tentacles, infusing the creatures that serve it, even tangentially, with vitality and protection from harm.
Diabolic Vigor.hazardDisable: @Check[religion|dc:30] (expert) to pray for divine intervention in counterbalancing this infernal influence; @Check[arcana|dc:35] (expert), @Check[nature|dc:35] (expert), or @Check[occultism|dc:35] (expert) to exert a magical force of will greater than the gate's influence; @Check[athletics|dc:38] (expert) or Thievery (expert) to disrupt the pentagram surrounding the Inferno Gate; or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (7th rank; counteract DC 30) to cut off the magical energies. Magical checks to disable this hazard can be attempted from up to 30 feet away from the Inferno Gate, but physical checks require physically touching the pentagram; three successes are required to disrupt the diabolic vigor hazard.
Diabolic Vigor.hazardRoutine: (1 action) On its turn, the diabolic vigor hazard empowers the merztorlegon and their bound armies within 200 feet of the Inferno Gate. It grants the siege devil regeneration 20 and reduces their weakness to holy from 20 to 10. The armies gain regeneration 10 and reduce their weakness to area damage and splash damage by 5. These effects last for 1 round.
Diabolic Vigor.name: Diabolic Vigor

BGU487rQboeeEM4e.description: The disciple's Strikes deal an additional 2d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.
BGU487rQboeeEM4e.name: Sneak Attack

TopeqZhd040eTV30.description:
Trigger An adjacent creature uses a manipulate action or a move action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a move action it's using

Effect The disciple drives several threaded needles through the triggering creature's clothing and pulls, momentarily binding its outfit and restricting movement. The disciple attempts a @Check[Tailoring Lore] check against the triggering creature's AC. If the triggering creature isn't wearing at least a cloak, sash, tabard, or similar amount of visible cloth, apply a –2 circumstance penalty to this check.

Critical Success As success, plus the disciple disrupts the action.

Success Threads partly entangle the triggering creature, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} and takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to it Speeds until the beginning of its next turn. Any creature within reach of the targeted creature can end these effects with an Interact action.

Failure The triggering creature is unaffected.

Critical Failure The disciple becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the beginning of their next turn.
TopeqZhd040eTV30.name: Sartorial Snag

dTtlbsapi0OxRW9w.description: While wearing clothing worth at least 10 gp, a disciple of thread can cause their sleeves or other parts of their outfit to extend and animate as unarmed Strikes in the flail weapon group. While wielding these sleeves, the cultist can use their Tailoring Lore modifier in place of Athletics to [[/act grapple skill=tailoring-lore]], [[/act reposition skill=tailoring-lore]], and [[/act trip skill=tailoring-lore]]. As a free action while carrying a tailoring toolkit, the disciple can Draw mundane sewing needles to use as lethal throwing weapons in the bow weapon group.
dTtlbsapi0OxRW9w.name: Tailor-Made Armaments

xQEEH3WAaepqhsRx.description: The disciple gains access to the critical specialization effects of their sleeve and needle Strikes, with a DC of 34.
xQEEH3WAaepqhsRx.name: Pins and Needles

3OBMYuGwBnj1yIPD.description: The divine warden army is a beacon for the faithful. A cleric of Iomedae can channel a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal} spell through a divine warden they can see within 60 feet. The cleric determines any targets or area for the spell as if they were standing in a space of the divine warden army of their choosing.
3OBMYuGwBnj1yIPD.name: Orchestra of Faith

5LBKi0slxTlpCZi0.description: Each time the divine warden army loses a segment and when they're reduced to 0 Hit Points, divine energy erupts from the fallen, dealing @Damage[8d6[spirit]|options:area-damage] damage to each enemy within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] (@Check[will|dc:38|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:enfeebled,inflicts:stupefied] save). On a failure, a creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 day (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} on a critical failure).
5LBKi0slxTlpCZi0.name: Divine Devastation

anYe0Rfu4UuxyNt2.description: The divine warden army unleashes beams of divine energy. This fusillade is a @Template[type:burst|distance:10] within 60 feet that deals @Damage[9d6[spirit]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:37|basic|traits:holy,magical] save. When the divine warden army is reduced to 2 segments, this area decreases to a @Template[type:burst|distance:5].
anYe0Rfu4UuxyNt2.name: Divine Lance Fusillade

xQgIoQdSRqQOY51E.description:
The divine wardens make coordinated melee attacks with their swords. Each enemy within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:37|basic] save. The damage depends on the number of actions.

1 @Damage[(2d8+1)[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage

2 @Damage[(4d8+12)[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage

3 @Damage[(6d8+13)[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage
xQgIoQdSRqQOY51E.name: Holy Blades

Dottari Excruciator Division.description:
The dottari serve as Cheliax's elite city guards, assembled and deployed to quash serious threats. Queen Abrogail Thrune I founded the original excruciator divisions to restore order to a nation torn by civil war and not yet fully submissive to Thrune rule. To this day, the dottari are empowered to destroy property (or break a few bones) in carrying out their duties.

Dottari are trained to neutralize foes nonlethally, but they empowered to use lethal force at their discretion (and often do). They're also famed for their alchemical crossbow bolts—many tipped with fast-acting, explosive glue—ending altercations before they've really begun.

5b2gROS9U3BUMTVc.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The excruciators make a coordinated effort to shove outward with their shields, taking down opponents and impediments alike. The troop attempts to either [[/act shove]] or [[/act trip]] each enemy in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] and [[/act force-open]] each object in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5]. The troop rolls a single Athletics check and compares the result to each target's appropriate DC. The troop doesn't take a penalty for not having a crowbar. It's possible for the troop to get a different degree of success for each target. The troop can't automatically Stride after any creature they successfully Shove.
5b2gROS9U3BUMTVc.name: Bash It Down

6OHVPrLywucNXKRj.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The excruciators swing their maces in a coordinated melee attack against each enemy in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] (@Check[reflex|dc:25|basic] save). The damage depends on the number of actions. The excruciators can choose to deal nonlethal damage with this attack.

1 @Damage[(1d6+2)[bludgeoning]]

2 @Damage[(2d6+11)[bludgeoning]]

3 @Damage[(3d6+14)[bludgeoning]]
6OHVPrLywucNXKRj.name: Beat the Lawbreakers

CfGBij51po7bDROg.description:
Trigger A creature adjacent to the dottari excruciator division leaves a square during a move action it's using

Effect The excruciators deal @Damage[(2d8+9)[bludgeoning]] damage to the triggering creature with a @Check[reflex|dc:25|basic] save. On a critical failure, the creature's move action is disrupted.
CfGBij51po7bDROg.name: Long Arm of the Law

OFhSDDlpQpjidJ59.description: The excruciators draw or reload their crossbows with special hindering bolts, then launch a ranged attack in the form of a volley. This volley is a @Template[type:burst|distance:10] within 80 feet that deals @Damage[4d6[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:25|basic] save). When the dottari excruciator division is reduced to 2 or fewer segments, this area decreases to a @Template[type:burst|distance:5]. On a failure, a creature also takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds for 1 round. On a critical failure, a creature also gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} condition ([[/act escape dc=25]]).
OFhSDDlpQpjidJ59.name: Stop Where You Are

Dottari Excruciator Division.name: Dottari Excruciator Division

Dream Drowner.description: Dream drowners are anemone-like predators from Orv's flooded vaults. A dream drowner indefinitely parasitizes and mentally controls a host to serve as its mount as it seeks out the thoughts of thinking prey to consume. So far, any attempt to communicate with these creatures elicits aggression, yet the beings' behavior demonstrates extraordinary intelligence.

3m1oxWgbOCdE244Q.description: A creature affected by a dream drowner's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.OsOhx3TGIZ7AhD0P]{Dominate} spell becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 minute after the dominate spell ends. The creature can attempt a @Check[will|dc:32] save at the end of each of its turns to end the condition.
3m1oxWgbOCdE244Q.name: Entangled Thoughts

OL2lhDAzH2liCDwa.description: When a creature fails or critically fails a Will save against a dream drowner's occult innate spells, the creature takes @Damage[1d6[mental]|traits:nonlethal]{1d6 nonlethal mental} damage per rank of the spell.
OL2lhDAzH2liCDwa.name: Mind Leech

Pe8iOQ2bZXQ8FGIk.description:
A dream drowner assaults the minds of distracted creatures. Each creature within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] that has the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} or stupefied condition takes @Damage[10d8[mental]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[will|dc:32|basic] save).

The dream drowner can't use this ability again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge this ability]]{1d4 rounds}.
Pe8iOQ2bZXQ8FGIk.name: Subjugate Minds

SrGNPrzi2VPpra0J.description:
30 feet.

The dream drowner's tentacles move with hypnotic grace. When a creature ends its turn in the dream drowner's aura, it must attempt a @Check[will|dc:32] save, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} on a failure (or increasing its stupefied value by 1, to a maximum of 4). The dream drowner can deactivate or activate this aura by using a single action, which has the concentrate trait.
SrGNPrzi2VPpra0J.name: Entrancing Movement

Sweet hags use bright colors, pleasant visages, and sugary treats to draw in children and the young at heart. Their favorite prey is impoverished youngsters who are unlikely to be missed—sweet hags offer them food and a veneer of kindness before devouring the hapless child. Sweet hags also enchant their food to magically charm others, often using these bespelled servitors to handle all of their busywork. Though they present a lovely and generous face to the world, they turn vicious when insulted or defied. A sweet hag's true form is a dribbling mass of flesh with gumdrop eyes, often resembling melting taffy.

Hags are malevolent predators who use magic and manipulation to lure children and young adults into their clutches. Though their true forms are eldritch and horrifying, hags spend much of their lives disguised as ordinary women. They seek out targets who are unhappy, innocent, or otherwise vulnerable, preying on their weaknesses before snatching them up. The typical hag is abusive, controlling, and narcissistic. Gorthoklek.description:
When an army of devils invades to bathe a region in bloodshed and hellfire, it is likely that one of the nessaris masterminded the incursion. Cunning, powerful, and ruthless, nessaris often serve the archdevils directly. They rule infernal duchies, subjugate mortal worlds, and usurp infernal rivals using unparalleled despotism and calculated ferocity. To realize their tyrannical machinations, nessaris claim mortal souls that they corrupt into ort servants, which can then be shaped and transformed through infernal manipulation into the terrifying devils that form Hell's formidable legions. They often select the most wicked and vicious orts for their armies, drawing upon these lesser devils' depravity during powerful magical ceremonies to create hideous and terrifying abominations that can cow and eviscerate the nessari's enemies.

Each nessari is crafted deep within the nightmarish bowels of Nessus, the ninth layer of Hell, to serve the whims of archdevils and infernal dukes. Those nessaris that don't leave Nessus to command infernal legions in the upper layers of Hell often form the courts of Hell's elite, gathering cronies and sects that shape Hell's political landscape through subterfuge and manipulation. But many nessaris see themselves as living embodiments of hellfire, the all-encompassing wrath of Hell, and thus prefer to dwell in realms consumed by fire. In Avernus, Dis, Malebolge, Nessus, and Phlegethon, nessaris build vast citadels of brimstone wreathed in flame to lord over.

Rather than being above the constant power struggles of the diabolic ranks, nessaris are in the thick of it. Even apocalyptic schemes to conquer or despoil mortal worlds usually begin from a desire to claw a single rank up the immortal hierarchy of Hell. For this reason, the best, yet also most dangerous, ally against a nessari is the nessari next to them.

Nessaris tower over other devils, standing at least 16 feet tall, weighing over 1,000 pounds, and brandishing wingspans in excess of 20 feet.

Infernal Dukes

Elite members of Hell's political infrastructure and leadership hierarchy, the dukes of Hell are chosen from among the most tyrannical, oppressive, and conniving devils. While not all infernal dukes are nessaris, a nessari's natural disposition toward conquest and oppression often makes them an ideal candidate for this position. To create an infernal duke, adjust the nessari to be between 21st and 25th level. Because of their physical prowess, manipulative nature, and powerful spellcasting abilities, infernal dukes make excellent villains for long-running campaigns.

Masters of corruption and architects of conquest, devils seek both to tempt mortal life to join in their pursuit of all things profane and to spread tyranny throughout all worlds. The temptations they offer mortals range from great powers granted by the signing of an infernal contract to twisted favors following a whispered pledge to a diabolic patron, or any number of even subtler exchanges. Those who succumb to these temptations find themselves consigned to an afterlife of endless torment in the pits of Hell, wherein the only hope of escape lies in the chance of being promoted to become a devil in the infernal ranks.

Every devil has a specific role to play in the upkeep of the remorseless bureaucratic machine that is Hell, from soldiers and scholars to inquisitors, lawyers, judges, and executioners. Lowly orts perform subservient labor to more powerful and specialized devils, such as infantry and contract devils, while the greatest nessaris command entire infernal armies.

Asmodeus stands at the apex of the structure he created, but the layers below him are marked by a constant jockeying for position. Most diabolic plans ultimately serve to improve the schemer's place in the hierarchy.

The monologue ends (and the bonuses are lost) if Grachius becomes unable to act or speak, or if he ends his turn without having taken this action.
5Wz0WQ1PV14QRSd9.name: Monologue

g8R8ggVM05eTvzXw.description:
Trigger Grachius would be reduced to 0 HP

Requirements Grachius has a divine immolation spell remaining

Effect Grachius refuses to disappoint Abrogail Thrune; he stabilizes at 1 HP just long enough to cast divine immolation, centered on himself. He dies, immolated in the hellish flames.
g8R8ggVM05eTvzXw.name: Unyielding Purpose

oPQTN3S99XiRLI4G.description: If the next action Grachius uses is to Cast a Spell, the spell ignores 20 resistance to energy damage. This applies to all damage the spell deals, including persistent damage and damage caused by an ongoing effect of the spell. A creature's immunities are unaffected.
oPQTN3S99XiRLI4G.name: Overwhelming Energy

Greater Hellcat.description:
Hellcats are devious predators native to the fiery pits of Hell. While the fiendish creatures resemble undead skeletal smilodons, bones smoking with heat and dripping with boiling blood, they're actually living hellspawn whose transparent flesh reveals their burning skeleton. A typical hellcat is 9 feet long and weighs 1,000 pounds.

Left to their own devices, hellcats spend their time hunting. As fiendish creatures, they don't need mortal sustenance but devour prey for the sheer pleasure of inflicting pain. They're also far more intelligent than most assume, and they resent being treated as unintelligent animals; those who treat a hellcat thusly might find themselves made into a trophy for its pack, as a hellcat will go to great lengths to coordinate elaborate revenge upon any who fail to show them proper respect.

Though they can't speak, hellcats know Diabolic and can communicate by telepathy with any creature capable of speech. They rarely say much except to whisper threats and acknowledge the orders of their diabolic masters.

Hellcats are quick to retreat if clearly outmatched or up against foes they're unable to reach, but they never forget prey that escapes them.

9q34cCv2FZ9uAGeu.description: The greater hellcat Strides and makes a Strike at the end of that movement. If the greater hellcat began this action @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden}, it remains hidden until after the ability's Strike.
9q34cCv2FZ9uAGeu.name: Pounce

GGXabOo5laUxY2kn.description:
This functions as telepathy, except that the greater hellcat can speak mentally to any creature, regardless of language. This doesn't grant the greater hellcat the ability to understand what the other creature is thinking, unless that creature also understands Diabolic.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.Telepathy]
GGXabOo5laUxY2kn.name: Fiendish Telepathy 100 feet

MQq8mozf2GsgGMaD.description:
The greater hellcat produces a low growl to disorient and frighten foes. The hellcat can cause this vocalization to originate from somewhere else within 30 feet. Non-fiends in a @Template[type:burst|distance:15] must attempt a @Check[will|dc:37] save. The hellcat can't issue another Menacing Growl for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 24 hours.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4}.
MQq8mozf2GsgGMaD.name: Menacing Growl

QHjQVrs9rgntyLlW.description: The hellcat deals an additional 3d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened} creatures.
QHjQVrs9rgntyLlW.name: Fearful Attack

Xu7t2hv6lxIZkRCM.description:
Trigger The greater hellcat is critically hit by any Strike

Effect The greater hellcat's Menacing Growl recharges. The creature that dealt the triggering Strike must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:37] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4} on a critical failure).
Xu7t2hv6lxIZkRCM.name: Vengeful Growl

ekEhxxOdLwJptDnc.description: The greater hellcat telepathically links its senses to all other hellcats within 100 feet for 10 minutes. It loses this contact with any hellcat that moves out of a 100-foot radius. While linked to at least one ally, the greater hellcat can't be flanked and gains a +2 status bonus to Will saving throws.
ekEhxxOdLwJptDnc.name: Hell Pack Mindlink

uZezbckq3nAKneY8.description: A greater hellcat can live within the fears of others and use their dread to hide from sight. The greater hellcat can [[/act hide]] in the presence of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened} creatures. If successful, the greater hellcat becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} from frightened creatures as if it moved behind cover or into concealment, but must otherwise Hide normally from non-frightened creatures.
uZezbckq3nAKneY8.name: Elusive Terror

Greater Hellcat.name: Greater Hellcat
Greater Hellcat.npcAllSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

Guardian Guises.description: Apparitions of Aroden in his various 12 guises (the shepherd, soldier, tailor, thief, and more) emerge in pairs to defend this room.
Guardian Guises.hazardDisable: @Check[diplomacy|dc:43] (master), @Check[intimidation|dc:43] (master), or @Check[religion|dc:43] (expert); three successes are required to convince the trap that Aroden is truly dead, causing the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.jQdm301h6e8hIY4U]{Spiritual Guardians} to hesitate and protest before fading away
Guardian Guises.hazardReset: 1 day or after Kaisentia spends 10 minutes here in focused prayer
Guardian Guises.hazardRoutine: (2 actions; spirit) The hazard Sustains both @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.jQdm301h6e8hIY4U]{spiritual guardians}, either attacking or protecting at Kaisentia's direction. Once per round, if fewer than two spiritual guardians are present, the hazard conjures one new spiritual guardian from one of the statues as an action. Each statue can create only one spiritual guardian in this way before needing to be reset.
Guardian Guises.name: Guardian Guises

Haunted Knife Collection.description: Crates of knives and daggers shine with ill intent.
Haunted Knife Collection.hazardDisable: @Check[religion|dc:26] (master) to exorcise the spirits, @Check[crafting|dc:33] (expert) to damage the knives, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (5th rank; counteract DC 29) to counteract the crate
Haunted Knife Collection.hazardReset: The spirits in the hazard reactivate after 10 minutes.
Haunted Knife Collection.hazardRoutine: (3 actions) The knife collection identifies targets. It first moves to have as many living creatures in its space as possible within a single Fly action, then attempts dagger Strikes against living creatures in its space.
Haunted Knife Collection.name: Haunted Knife Collection

1BwV9TFJ4LsBz1jc.description: The hellfire hydra slams each of its heads into the ground, where they explode before quickly reforming. The hellfire hydra creates a number of @Template[type:burst|distance:5]s within 10 feet equal to its current number of heads. These bursts can't overlap. Each creature in a burst takes @Damage[6d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:40|basic] save). This counts as a number of attacks equal to the number of heads the hellfire hydra has toward the hydra's multiple attack penalty.
1BwV9TFJ4LsBz1jc.name: Conflagration of Jaws

1Kn4bOqRAwlByCBN.description: The hellfire hydra ignores the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} condition from smoke.
1Kn4bOqRAwlByCBN.name: Smoke Vision

8x2IcnPppFO2sxj1.description:
A hellfire hydra has five heads. A creature can attempt to sever one of the hydra's heads by specifically targeting it and dealing damage equal to the head's Hit Points. A head that isn't completely severed returns to full Hit Points at the end of any creature's turn.

A hellfire hydra can regrow a severed head using hellfire regeneration. A creature can prevent this regrowth by dealing damage to the stump with a cold or water effect, snuffing out its flames. Single-target cold or water effects need to be targeted at a specific stump, but effects that deal splash damage or affect areas covering the hellfire hydra's whole space snuff out all stumps if they deal damage and have the cold or water trait. If the attack that destroys a head deals any damage with the cold or water trait, the stump is snuffed out instantly. If all five heads are snuffed out, the hydra dies.

Hydra Head

  • Hit Points 50

  • Immunities Area Damage

  • Weaknesses Cold 15, Holy 10, Water 10

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.QigGoOYUG7BHuvE4]{Effect: Hellfire Hydra Heads}
8x2IcnPppFO2sxj1.name: Head Regrowth

G19fmy4N3CMCCkXz.description: A hellfire hydra gains an extra reaction per round for each of its heads beyond the first, which it can use only to make Reactive Strikes. It can't use more than 1 reaction on the same triggering action, even if a creature leaves several squares within its reach, and the hydra must use a different head for each Reactive Strike it makes. Whenever one of the hellfire hydra's heads is destroyed, the hydra loses 1 of its extra reactions per round.
G19fmy4N3CMCCkXz.name: Reactive Heads

pRi7gYr2YwTJuHxE.description:
The hellfire hydra has regeneration equal to 5 × the number of heads it has. If a hellfire hydra's body is missing any heads and the remaining stumps haven't been snuffed out, the hydra attempts a @Check[fortitude|dc:42] save after it regains Hit Points from regeneration. On a success, one non-snuffed stump regrows two heads; on a critical success, two nonsnuffed stumps regrow into two heads each. The hellfire hydra can never grow more than 10 heads. The hellfire hydra's regeneration only fully deactivates if all its heads are destroyed and all stumps are snuffed out, at which point it dies.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.Regeneration]
pRi7gYr2YwTJuHxE.name: Hellfire Regeneration

Hellfire Tornado.description: The very air catches fire from the heat of a dragon's breath, causing a burning tornado.
Hellfire Tornado.hazardDisable: The Hellfire tornado can't be disabled—only endured. It ends after 5 rounds.
Hellfire Tornado.hazardReset: Once 5 rounds pass, the Hellfire tornado dissipates and doesn't reset.
Hellfire Tornado.hazardRoutine:
(1 action; air, fire) The Hellfire tornado—a 15-footdiameter column 80 feet tall—moves 60 feet down the street. It can move through creatures' spaces, and creatures can move into its space, though the tornado's space is difficult terrain. Each creature the tornado moves through or each creature that ends its turn in the tornado's area takes @Damage[(4d10)[bludgeoning],(4d6)[fire]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:40|basic|traits:air,fire] save). A creature can be affected by the tornado only once per round.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and rises 10 feet into the air as it's engulfed by the tornado ([[/act escape dc=40]]). While engulfed, a creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}, and if it doesn't have a fly Speed, it gains a 10-foot fly Speed until it either reaches the ground or ceases to be in the tornado's area, potentially falling when the hazard ends or when it leaves the tornado's area. A creature engulfed by the tornado moves along with it on the tornado's turn.

Critical Failure As failure, except the creature takes double damage and rises 20 feet into the air.
Hellfire Tornado.name: Hellfire Tornado

6OHVRvmoEsZdu9J2.description:
Trigger The amalgamite is hit by a Strike

Effect The amalgamite Repositions itself or Transposes itself with another creature. If the amalgamite successfully Transposes its location, it and any transposed creature take half damage from the triggering Strike.
6OHVRvmoEsZdu9J2.name: Displace

AZRHnzhMZcOnRRFV.description:
40 feet.

A creature that begins its turn within the area feels its body begin to stretch and must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:33] save or become destabilized. A destabilized creature emits a 10-foot destabilizing field aura and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}. The destabilization ends when the creature is no longer sickened. A creature that succeeds at its saving throw against the aura is temporarily immune to all destabilizing fields for 1 minute.
AZRHnzhMZcOnRRFV.name: Destabilizing Field

BtXNJtlQV7SnjiyG.description: The amalgamite teleports into an unoccupied space it can see within 50 feet.
BtXNJtlQV7SnjiyG.name: Reposition

hkruqo5TH8dgoePl.description: The amalgamite chooses up to two destabilized creatures it can see within 50 feet and swaps their positions, or moves one such creature to an unoccupied space it can see within range. If the amalgamite chooses two creatures, it can choose itself as a target, but both targets must be the same size. An unwilling creature can attempt a @Check[will|dc:33] save. If either target succeeds at this saving throw, both are unaffected.
hkruqo5TH8dgoePl.name: Transpose

Hellknight Dragoon Squad.description: Some fugitives are so dangerous or numerous that they warrant a whole Hellknight squadron who can ride after quarry and dismount to give chase in crowded settlements. These Hellknights wield flails as capably as they wield fear, using both to subdue and restrain foes.

IVVQNnLlawzqFTYA.description:

10 feet.

UcAL6U3amw64JFv3.name: Arrow Volley

X0RMAYFeESgrAaxL.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The dragoons attempt to [[/act demoralize]] all foes in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:15], comparing the result of a single Intimidation check to each target's Will DC. The squad doesn't take the penalty if they don't speak the same language as a target. It's possible for the dragoon squad to get a different degree of success for each target, and a target is temporarily immune to this ability only if the squad critically fails the check against them.
X0RMAYFeESgrAaxL.name: Fear the Chain

gP9xV4BDHAN65B94.description:
Trigger A creature or troop adjacent to the dragoon squad gains the frightened condition, or an adjacent troop is reduced to 2 segments

Effect Sensing their foes' faltering morale, the dragoons lash out with their manacles. The triggering creature must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:25] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} until the end of the squad's next turn.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} until the end of the squad's next turn and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} until it [[/act escape dc=25]]{Escapes}.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} instead of immobilized.
gP9xV4BDHAN65B94.name: Bind Them in Chains

Hellknight Dragoon Squad.name: Hellknight Dragoon Squad
Hellknight Dragoon Squad.npcAllSaves: +2 circumstance bonus to saves vs fear effects

Hellknight Hunter Squad.description: Against immense prey, Order of the Pike Hellknights assemble elite squads trained to strike as one, shield each other from fiery breath, protect civilians, and stand strong against foes that would terrify lesser troops.

1NirhglyYLZu46Mn.description: The squad's members throw a volley of javelins. Each creature in a @Template[type:burst|distance:10] within 30 feet of the troop takes @Damage[(5d6+9)[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:33|basic] save. When the Hellknight hunters are reduced to 2 segments, this area decreases to a @Template[type:burst|distance:5].
1NirhglyYLZu46Mn.name: Hurl Javelins

5kkVqFmwF22sySq8.description: The Hellknights defensively lock their shields. Until the start of this troop's next turn, the troop and all allies within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] gain a +1 circumstance bonus to their AC and Reflex saving throws.
5kkVqFmwF22sySq8.name: Disciplined Barricade

5sU5KauL79M1suJI.description: The hunters bandage an adjacent creature. The target regains @Damage[(5d8+20)[healing]] Hit Points, after which the target is immune to this ability for 1 day.
5sU5KauL79M1suJI.name: Medic!

Fj8tpGHJ19jguRyj.description: Hellknight hunters can use Monster Lore to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about creatures of any type. Fj8tpGHJ19jguRyj.name: Hunters of Monsters

VF0wsOMDhXVJG1Qe.description:
Frequency once per round

VF0wsOMDhXVJG1Qe.name: Phalanx Strike

yDs95reKF7jUx74n.name: Pin It Down

Hellknight Hunter Squad.name: Hellknight Hunter Squad

Requirements Your Strikes currently deal extra damage from your champion's reaction.

Make a Strike against the creature that triggered your champion's reaction. If you hit, double the extra damage the target takes from your reaction, and the target must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:40] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}. Regardless of the result, the creature is temporarily immune to your Gruesome Strike for 24 hours.
TOWOiERSoIqw44E3.name: Gruesome Strike

TVJn7DPNUO3Lmdwc.description:
With the protection of your shield, you dive into battle! You Raise your Shield and Stride. If you end your movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, you can make a melee Strike against that enemy.

You can use Defensive Advance while Burrowing, Climbing, Flying, or Swimming instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.
TVJn7DPNUO3Lmdwc.name: Defensive Advance

pG5dN4QhEOKrGftC.description: You're surrounded by an aura in a 15-foot emanation. It has the aura and divine traits. Any follower of your deity within the aura immediately knows you're a champion of your deity. This aura is used as the range for your champion's reaction and for various other effects. You can suppress or resume the aura as a single action, which has the concentrate trait, and it ends if you fall @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}.
pG5dN4QhEOKrGftC.name: Champion's Aura

rdOYgMFeiBhVzcBu.description:
Trigger An enemy in your champion's aura damages you

Effect You put an impertinent foe who dared harm you in their proper place. You command each enemy in your champion's aura to kneel before you in obedience. If they dare to refuse, they must pay the price in pain and anguish. The enemy must choose one of the following options.

  • Kneel The enemy drops @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} as a free action.

  • Refuse You deal @Damage[(5d6)[mental],(5)[persistent,mental]] damage to the enemy.

Regardless of which option the enemy chose, your Strikes against it deal 3 extra spirit damage until the end of your next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feat-effects.Item.2a6fuugiPpICe3Li]{Effect: Champion's Extra Damage}
rdOYgMFeiBhVzcBu.name: Exalted Iron Command

Hellknight Sea Brigade.description:
A Hellknight cavalry brigade consists of several Hellknights and a single field-maralictor, all wearing the distinctive armor of their order and wielding lances. The maralictor speaks for the brigade, questioning travelers the brigade encounters and barking orders. A Hellknight brigade is typically based at a keep or other fortification controlling an area measured by a day's ride in every direction—about 25 miles. Farther-ranging missions are possible but require substantial logistical support.

A military serves to defend and fight on behalf of nations and can be trained and deployed in various ways.

V5g0qZhLRkme45qX.description:
Requirements The Hellknights are on a ship

Effect The Hellknights throw a volley of grappling hooks at a 10-foot-radius burst within 30 feet. Five grappling hooks landing at random squares in the burst take hold, and the Hellknights heave, forcibly moving both ships up to 15 feet toward each other until they're adjacent to each other. The ships remain adjacent to each other until all five of the grappling hooks are dislodged (each as an Interact action) or their respective chains are broken (Hardness 8, HP 20, BT 10).
V5g0qZhLRkme45qX.name: Boarding Grapple

VlIh7APIScILudOU.description: The ship crew ignores the penalty for attacking while on a vehicle that has moved in the last round and takes only a –2 penalty if the vehicle is uncontrolled or used an action with the reckless trait.
VlIh7APIScILudOU.name: Sea Legs

iFIgoidhd52BmiLu.description: Whenever a troop moves, you move one of its segments and the other segments follow behind it. At the end of the movement, you can group the other segments adjacent to the one you moved as you see fit, provided none of them moves farther than the moving segment. If you choose not to move the troop any distance, you can instead reshape the position of all the segments as long as one stays in place.
iFIgoidhd52BmiLu.name: Troop Movement

iKR8M3h9wCtVtDTe.description:
1 to 3

88EzuCJDr2tyg96M.name: Hellish Spears

B2xSj2M2JBt6C0XP.description: These soldiers have had it beaten into them that they shall hold their ground no matter what. If any effect would force the House Thrune elite infantry to move, reduce that distance by 10 feet. Any time it would be affected by the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} condition, the elite infantry is instead @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} for the same duration.
B2xSj2M2JBt6C0XP.name: Give No Ground

cbAUIdcOFndv1kHX.description: As long as it has 4 segments, the House Thrune elite infantry troop improves its degree of success on rout checks by one step, even when without a commander. When it has three segments, it instead gains a +2 status bonus to rout checks.
cbAUIdcOFndv1kHX.name: Hell's Will

vflRjjd5NHRkgg3m.description: The House Thrune elite infantry unit draws, loads, and fires a barrage from its crossbows. The salvo is a @Template[type:burst|distance:10] within 100 feet that deals @Damage[5d8[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic] save). When the elite infantry is reduced to 2 segments, this area decreases to a @Template[type:burst|distance:5].
vflRjjd5NHRkgg3m.name: Crossbow Array

vj9Tir2Y4G9lHyJb.description: The House Thrune elite infantry charges forward with an infernal yell on cloven hooves. The troop Strides up to twice its Speed. At the end of the troop's movement, each enemy within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] takes @Damage[(2d6+7)[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:34|basic] save.

If successful, the chains keep the target grappled or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} for 1 minute, until the target [[/act escape dc=33]]{Escapes}, or until the chains are destroyed (Hardness 10, 30 HP), whichever comes first.
8khipjo5faWmqtx2.name: Hell's Arrest

ghw3XeJ0Vz2PJhqX.description: Ignaro is bound to a phistophilus in Erebus. When Ignaro dies, his body disintegrates and his soul is sent to Hell. All weapons that he wields deal an additional @Damage[1d6[spirit]] damage with the unholy trait.
ghw3XeJ0Vz2PJhqX.name: Hell's Own Servitor

ks8skGnYYOGHBixh.description: Ignaro declares an object he can see within 30 feet to be heretical. After smoldering for 1 round, it's engulfed in flames, taking @Damage[3d6[persistent,fire]] damage that ignores half of the object's Hardness. Immersion in water for 1 round ends the damage, as does the object being splashed with a flask of holy water. Any other water effect that isn't just mundane water used against the object can attempt to counteract the effect (DC 30). If this ability destroys an object, Ignaro gains temporary Hit Points equal to twice the object's level (minimum 2) that last for 1 minute.
ks8skGnYYOGHBixh.name: Ignite Heresy

Infernal Bow Shocks.description: Wave after wave of Hellish power ripples out from the pentagram surrounding the Inferno Gate, bathing all of the battling armies around it in its dark energies. Some are slain on the spot, while others fall into cracks that open beneath them in the earth, and still others are consumed by ignited gasses.
Infernal Bow Shocks.hazardDisable:
@Check[Devil Lore|dc:34] or @Check[HellLore|dc:34] to give the proper incantations and invoke the name of Visperthul to ward off the magical defenses from the Inferno Gate; @Check[arcana|dc:38] (expert), @Check[nature|dc:38] (expert), @Check[occultism|dc:38] (expert), or @Check[religion|dc:38] (expert) to erect a magical barrier to shield against the power emanating from the gate; @Check[survival|dc:43] to use the natural terrain as a shield to survive the onslaught of magical energies; @Check[will|dc:48] save to simply push back against the Hellish storm surge and refute them; or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (9th rank; counteract DC 34) to blast the bow shock with magic to stem its flow; three successes are required to dissipate the hazard's energies.

The first time a PC successfully uses Devil Lore or Hell Lore against this hazard, all PCs gain a +2 status bonus to their saving throws against the hazard's effects.
Infernal Bow Shocks.hazardRoutine: (2 actions) The infernal bow shocks release a different effect each round for 3 rounds, centered on a randomly-chosen PC each time and never the same PC twice in a row (though creatures standing near each other might just be unlucky). In the first round, it unleashes Flaming Fumes. In the second round, it uses an 8th-rank whispers of the void spell (DC 38), and in the third round, it emulates the effect of an earthquake spell (DC 38), with each of the three piles of tower rubble collapsing as though they were shoddy structures. Notably, no fissures extend into the former inner bailey of Fort Arego (area E4, as outlined by the remaining rectangular battlements). The hazard concludes for the PCs when it's disabled, or when the third round ends.
Infernal Bow Shocks.name: Infernal Bow Shocks

Infernal Tide.description: Sarglagons can gather to form an infernal tide, a troop that displays unnerving fluidity in the way its devils seem to flow around each other.

005Eo5g7OKNU629Q.description:

The infernal tide conjures murky water to fill the lungs of all creatures that can't breathe water within a @Template[type:cone|distance:30]. Each target in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:30] save.

A trio of brilliant gems have been set into this elegant golden crown. You gain a +3 item bonus to checks to Recall Knowledge, regardless of the skill. You must select skills and languages the first time you invest the crown, and whenever you invest the same crown of intellect, you get the same skills and languages you chose the first time.

Activate—Search Your Mind 1 (concentrate)

piaI2WIRMXRCEjxf.name: Channeling Block

Majordomo Cizoboseth.description:
Where a bright mind seeking knowledge becomes corrupted by eloquent lies and twisted truths, an ayngavhaul is sure to lurk. Often donned in the holy vestments of other faiths in a twisted mockery of their principles, these wily, well-read devils delight in using their knowledge to twist religious texts and teachings into the dangerous principles those same texts warn against. While many ayngavhauls develop advanced knowledge of unique specializations, there are many whose depth of knowledge of a single religion rivals that of even the most wizened priests.

Any information an ayngavhaul has read or learned is added to a massive living tome unique to the ayngavhaul. The information contained sorts itself based on the topic and point its owner is making.

While these devils spend most of their time in the libraries of Hell, they are most often summoned in desperate bids by students seeking lost or forbidden knowledge, and such knowledge comes with a cost. These devils use truths and loose interpretations of texts to lend credence to their heretical viewpoints. When these once-bright intellectuals are corrupted into blasphemous priests, tyrants, and despots spreading the twisted words of an ayngavhaul, that devil gains influence and renown within the scholarly circles of Hell.

46dLIVM7cpDD53uS.description: Cizoboseth keeps records of palace events and accounts in a personal archive, a floating collection of ledgers constantly revolving around him. Retrieving or returning a ledger requires an Interact action.
46dLIVM7cpDD53uS.name: Personal Archive

Igt88kb16Bk6ajJg.description: Creatures hit by Cizoboseth's searing words must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:37] saving throw or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 round (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} on a critical failure). If the target is trained in Religion, it takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its save.
Igt88kb16Bk6ajJg.name: Poison Minds

jUAtoBpUZQvKebon.description:
Trigger Cizoboseth is targeted by a spell

Effect Cizoboseth flings a ledger from his personal archive at the spell. He attempts a @Check[flat|dc:5]. On a success, the ledger fully absorbs the effects of the spell and burns up into a harmless pile of ash. Regardless of the result, Cizoboseth can't use this ability again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge this ability]]{1d4 rounds}.
jUAtoBpUZQvKebon.name: Spellblock Ledger

An affected creature takes @Damage[3d10[mental]|options:area-damage] damage plus @Damage[3d10[spirit]|options:area-damage] damage and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:37] save. Affected creatures gain a cumulative +1 circumstance bonus (up to a total of +4) to saves against all future attempts to Herald Heresy for 1 minute, as they become inured to the blasphemies.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune for 1 hour.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2}.

TzNeLGCVqEmBo8Kj.description:
Mareshiah produces an infernal contract for a single living mortal. This contract can grant a wide range of abilities and effects, akin to the power of a wish ritual but fulfilled to the letter by Mareshiah. To receive any of those benefits, the mortal must willingly sign their true name to the contract. At that point, the mortal's soul is bound to Mareshiah and Hell.

While the contract is in effect, the victim can't be restored to life except by a wish ritual or similar magic. If the mortal is restored to life by those means, Mareshiah knows which mortal came to life and can locate the creature or creatures who restored the mortal to life for 1 year, gaining the effects of a pinpoint spell. Avoiding the terms of an infernal contract is difficult and often dangerous.
TzNeLGCVqEmBo8Kj.name: Draft Contract

cbaULlUeMrNNbwGU.description: A signed contract carried by Mareshiah (including draped over her horns) is immune to damage from all creatures other than her. Mareshiah is immune to mental effects that would make them destroy, nullify, or alter a contract.
cbaULlUeMrNNbwGU.name: Ward Contract

The wounds from Mareshiah's Strikes resist healing.

A spellcaster or item attempting to use healing magic on a creature damaged by Mareshiah's Strikes must first attempt to counteract infernal wound (DC 42). If it isn't counteracted, the healing has no effect.

SnViOjtyu4ZATbvi.name: Borrow Time

Merztorlegon.description: Merztorlegons are walking siege engines, their bodies bristling with ballistae and siege towers bolted to their shoulders. Their frontal armor leaves their back less defended, forcing Hell's commanders to support these juggernauts with infantry that can shield them from flanking strikes.

0FAz0uBOmKHv8Osa.description: A merztorlegon and their crew can [[/act demoralize]] creatures at a range of 120 feet and don't take a penalty for not sharing a language with the target.
0FAz0uBOmKHv8Osa.name: Besieging Fury

1ExfVEDmSjYf6o9H.description: A merztorlegon's melee Strikes deal an additional @Damage[3d12[untyped]] damage to items and structures.
1ExfVEDmSjYf6o9H.name: Sunder Structures

7IdpTl5O5Dni5LVO.description: The merztorlegon gathers a willing adjacent troop into their siege tower or shunts a stored troop into an adjacent space. The devil can store only one troop at a time, during which time the troop can't take actions, can't be targeted by effects, can be transported by the devil's translocate spell, and increases the damage dealt by Arrow Volley by 2d8. If the merztorlegon is defeated, any stored troop immediately reappears in or adjacent to the siege devil's space.
7IdpTl5O5Dni5LVO.name: Troop Transport

AelR3XQzsc9Brz6e.description: Several vordines inhabit the siege tower and are an extension of the merztorlegon, use the devil's skill modifiers, and can't be targeted individually. On the siege devil's turn, the crew can take 2 actions that can be used only to launch an Arrow Volley; [[/act demoralize]]; or to Aim, Load, or Launch the devil's shoulder ballista. Once the merztorlegon is reduced to half their maximum Hit Points, the siege crew is injured and takes only 1 action per turn.
AelR3XQzsc9Brz6e.name: Siege Crew

A shoulder ballista is an extension of the merztorlegon's body, functioning as a siege weapon that shares the demon's space, can't be targeted, and ceases to function after the merztorlegon's death. Trigger An adjacent creature whom the mannequin dealt damage to with a fist Strike since the beginning of the mannequin's last turn attempts to move away from the mannequin

Effect The mannequin dances after the triggering creature, either Climbing or Striding, following the creature and staying in reach throughout its movement until the creature stops moving or the mannequin has moved up to its full Speed, whichever happens first. The mannequin gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and Reflex saves against reactions triggered by its movement. If it critically succeeds at a Reflex save against a reaction triggered by its movement (or if the attacker critically fails its attack roll or check), the mannequin maneuvers the creature it's following so that the latter is exposed to the reaction; the attacker rerolls the attack roll or check against the followed creature or forces the followed creature to attempt a Reflex save against the reaction instead.
3XQkhOGtUD3EhhF4.name: Dance Partner

Nemyra.description:
Also called a hamadryad, a dryad queen rules over an entire forest, or a portion of an incredibly large forest, leading and protecting all dryads within. Dryad queens often have strange relationships with powerful and deadly fey, working together in a dualistic way despite their differences, with the queen representing nature's wonders and the other fey representing nature's wrath.

Nymphs are a family of fey that take the form of beautiful humanoids with elven features and have a deep association with the natural world. The most common of their kind are the dryads, which are spirits that embody great trees, but many other kinds of nymphs exist, including naiads, who watch over bodies of water. All nymphs are guardians of some element of nature, typically a specific tree or pond, or even-in the case of nymph queens-whole forests or massive bodies of water

Nymph Queens

Nymph queens are powerful nymphs who rule over entire regions of untouched wilderness, not just single trees or ponds. Every variety of nymph can have a queen. Naiad queens are among the most prominent, and more often interact with nearby mortals. Thus, some scholars refer to naiad queens as simply "nymphs."

7IWkM6MOEOAu4DTP.description:
A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.dileJ0Yxqg76LMvu]{One with Plants} spell cast by a dryad has an unlimited duration.

In addition, if the dryad merges with any tree in her domain, she can choose to instead enter an extradimensional living space within the tree, and can bring up to eight adjacent, willing creatures with her; the spell gains the extradimensional trait. The dryad can still be expelled from this space.
7IWkM6MOEOAu4DTP.name: Tree Meld

9OZuMP6qLeoyehVx.description:
30 feet. On a failed save, the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} in awe for 1 minute.

On a failed save, if the target was already affected by the dryad queen's beauty, the target can't use hostile actions against the dryad queen for 1 hour.

The nymph queen focuses her beauty upon a target, who must attempt a save against her nymph's beauty aura (@Check[will|dc:30] save). If the creature fails and was already affected by the aura, it takes a greater effect described in the nymph queen's entry.

A nymph queen can Focus Beauty on a given creature only once per turn.
D01DgsftPfTKC645.name: Focus Beauty

JYkKoCx49R8WXnXW.description: Nemyra is tied to the kelp forest in this room and treats the kelp as a tree for the purposes of her spells and abilities. Creatures that she summons with her @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.jSRAyd57kd4WZ4yE]{Summon Plant or Fungus} spell have the aquatic trait and a swim speed of 30 feet.
JYkKoCx49R8WXnXW.name: Tied to the Sea

Nymph queens can transform between their original form, which looks much like a typical nymph of their kind, and any Small or Medium humanoid form, typically choosing a more humanoid-looking version of their natural form.

afRIl1Q7FwNUtxuI.description: The dryad can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with animals and plants.
afRIl1Q7FwNUtxuI.name: Nature Empathy

jjcSFQRRi1OZjeeX.description:

Quelaunt.description:
This three-armed, three-legged monster has no discernible eyes, nose, ears, or mouth, and no visible means of ingesting food. Its limbs are distributed so evenly across its body that it's all but impossible to tell which way the creature is oriented at any given time. Few who witness a quelaunt linger on its alien looks for long though, as the invasion of their minds becomes a more pressing concern, sowing doubt, sorrow, and rage. This monstrosity not only delights in the negative emotions of its prey, but feeds on them, gaining strength and sustenance from their dismay. For the quelaunt, no act is too terrible or cruel to inflict on its victims, since the more a creature suffers, the more the quelaunt feasts.

Quelaunts are known to associate with other aberrant horrors, including jah-tohls and other creatures associated with the Dominion of the Black. However, the more prevalent theory paints them as more alien—perhaps invasive beings from another dimension of pure thought and feeling—and claims that in their natural state they have no physical bodies at all. Few dare speculate further; the only known autopsy of a quelaunt resulted in the researcher's suicide just days afterward and all the notes were mysteriously destroyed. Whatever secrets there are to be unlocked in the anatomy of these bizarre monsters are apparently important enough to warrant great protection from quelaunts, even after death.

Stygian Serpent.description:
These fabled beasts resemble massive snakes with long rows of finned spines down their back. Temperamental and territorial, sea serpents can capsize a boat with ease, and most won't hesitate to do so when hungry or threatened. Stories abound of aggrieved captains who spend their entire lives hunting down the elusive monster that sunk their ships and took their livelihoods. These hunts rely on rumors and glimpses of the beasts, as few survive the catastrophes wrought by sea serpents.

While many fishermen's tales paint sea serpents as divinely appointed guardians of the ocean or as evil and demonic agents, the truth is that most sea serpents are simply very large beasts with a knack for avoiding magical detection.

9jVKyOMk9msVj1hz.description: The sea serpent attempts to capsize an aquatic vessel of its size or smaller that it's adjacent to. The infernal registrar is a mortal representative of Hell's bureaucracy. They can access copies of all infernal contracts signed by a denizen of their world and can navigate the machinations of Hell's many devils. They can grant special access—for a price.

Larger societies rely on those with the authority and the ability to interpret and enforce laws. Some carry out these duties fairly, but others are harsh and cruel, imposing severe punishments on anyone unable to pay for clemency.

The infernal registrar will never promise a successful use of this ability in the agreements they make. Each agreement is typically for one attempt. Any copy summoned is simply a copy, has no impact on the original contract if destroyed or altered, and will vanish if taken more than 20 feet from the infernal registrar.

Success A copy of the contract appears before the infernal registrar after 1 hour.

CHqQHA8YIr6uIaZe.name: Request Document

Thephrol.description:
Gigantic loners, the great cyclopes are their lesser kin writ large. They're stronger and more violent, but their uncontrolled vision of possible futures has driven them beyond reason. They see every moment as a potential storm of uncontrollable fury and, out of a desperate desire for peace, quiet, and an end to their hunger, lash out at any who come near. Wise creatures avoid great cyclopes at all cost. It's fortunate for humanoids that great cyclopes prefer to dwell far from settlements.

Debate has long raged over the origins of these massive, destructive giants. They are so large that it had long been assumed they were used as beasts of burden by their lesser kin, now free to hunt and kill without restraint. Other scholars believe the great cyclops is the ultimate fate of the entire cyclops species. Whatever foolish decision or wayward curse caused the end of their civilization is still playing out, occasionally causing a cyclops to withdraw from their own kind, lose all semblance of intellect, and mutate into a lumbering, feral colossus.

The cyclopes are violent giants with a tragic past. Although they possess only one eye, they could once see far more than most, possessing occult wisdom and divinatory magic that gave them the mystic ability of foresight. But their legendary oracular powers failed to prevent the fall of their society, and the vast kingdoms of the cyclops long ago collapsed into ruin. Today, cyclopes have forgotten much of what they once knew, and they skulk among the crumbling remains of their fallen cities like forgotten kings and queens of their own fallen kingdoms.
